lesson.intro: Tidak semua bacaan harus dibaca kata demi kata. Skimming dan scanning membantu kamu membaca lebih cepat dengan tujuan yang jelas: skimming untuk memahami gambaran umum, dan scanning untuk menemukan informasi tertentu.

sections.heading: Skimming
sections.bodyMd: Saat **skim**, kamu membaca sekilas: judul, **headline**, paragraf pertama, dan paragraf terakhir. Tujuannya mendapat **overview** tentang isi teks. Kamu belum perlu memahami semua detail.

sections.heading: Scanning
sections.bodyMd: Saat **scan**, kamu mencari sesuatu yang spesifik: tanggal, nama, angka, atau **keyword**. Mata bergerak cepat sampai kamu bisa **locate** informasi itu, lalu baca kalimat di sekitarnya dengan teliti.

sections.heading: Menandai dan merangkum
sections.bodyMd: Gunakan **highlight** untuk kalimat penting, dan buat **outline** untuk urutan ide. Jangan menandai terlalu banyak, karena halaman yang penuh tanda sulit dibaca.

block3.title: Membaca Cepat dengan Tepat
block3.text:
Reading speed matters when you have a lot of material to cover. Two useful strategies are skimming and scanning. Skimming means that you glance quickly over a text to get an overview of its main ideas. You do not read every word. Instead, you look at the title, the headline, the first paragraph, and the last paragraph. These parts often reveal the purpose of the text.

Scanning is different. When you scan, you search for a specific piece of information, such as a date, a name, or a keyword. Your eyes move quickly down the page until you locate the item you need. Once you find it, you read the surrounding sentences carefully to understand its meaning.

Good readers often combine both strategies. They skim first to understand the structure, then use an outline in their notes to organize the main points. A short outline can show the order of the ideas and help the reader return to the important parts later. Some students also highlight key terms with a marker, but they should use this method carefully, because too much highlighting makes the page hard to read.

Speed alone is not the goal. A reader who moves quickly without understanding will miss important details. For this reason, it is useful to practise on short articles and ask yourself after each reading what the main point was. If you can answer clearly, your skimming is working well. If not, slow down and try again.

Many people use these strategies in everyday life. When you check the news on your phone, you skim the headlines. When you search a train schedule, you scan for the departure time. These habits are simple, but they make reading faster and more useful.
